key_insight: This paper consolidates the evolution of optimization methods into a practical taxonomy and evaluation protocol, revealing how choices of optimizers interact with scale, privacy constraints, and distributed setups to trade off convergence, generalization, and compute efficiency.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of unified guidance and standardized evaluations for choosing and tuning optimization algorithms across modern scenarios — large-scale models, differential privacy, and distributed training — where conventional optimizers (e.g., SGD, Adam) show distinct and sometimes conflicting limitations.
method: Survey and taxonomy: map historical and recent optimizer designs (first-order, adaptive, momentum variants) and categorize them by strengths/weaknesses.
Scenario-driven empirical evaluation: benchmark optimizers across representative settings (large-scale training, privacy-preserving SGD, and distributed/federated learning) using consistent metrics.
Practical protocols and recommendations: define evaluation metrics and configuration guidelines to select and tune optimizers depending on target trade-offs (speed, generalization, compute, privacy).
impact: Provides ML practitioners and system designers with an actionable framework to pick and tune optimizers for specific production constraints, improving training efficiency, robustness to privacy requirements, and scalability in distributed environments.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing evolution of optimizers (SGD → momentum → Adam → recent variants) with icons for key properties (adaptive, stable, memory-heavy).
Decision flowchart: select optimizer based on objectives (fast convergence, best generalization, DP constraints, distributed communication limits).
Multi-panel performance chart: side-by-side plots of convergence speed, test generalization, and compute cost across scenarios (large-scale, DP, distributed).
Illustration of trade-offs: triangle or radar chart visualizing convergence vs generalization vs computational/privacy cost for representative optimizers.
paper_title: Evolution of Optimization Methods: Algorithms, Scenarios, and Evaluations
paper_authors: Tong Zhang, Jiangning Zhang, Zhucun Xue, Juntao Jiang, Yicheng Xu
